The most pressing concern regarding superintelligence is the control problem. This problem arises because a superintelligent entity, by definition, would be vastly more intelligent than any human. One approach to the control problem is to design superintelligent systems with explicit safety mechanisms. These mechanisms could be built into the system's code, or they could be implemented through external control systems. The fundamental problem of economics is scarcity. Scarcity arises because our wants are unlimited, but the resources available to satisfy them are limited. The government may also regulate markets to prevent negative externalities, such as pollution.

The study of economics helps us understand how individuals, businesses, and governments make choices in the face of scarcity.
